newsitem.title: UK: U.S. shares in London steady, trading volume light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shares in London steady, trading volume light.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady on Monday with many participants sidelined following Wall Street's volatile session last Friday.
"There has been very little business this morning. Nobody is too sure where Wall Street is headed," one dealer said.
"The Dow showed a great deal of resilience on Friday so we could see it push ahead later today. But it's anyone's guess if the market will hold up this week or even by the end of the day."
On Friday, the Dow closed 0.86 higher after dropping nearly 90 points at its nadir after a Intel profits warning.
Intel, which plunged around eight percent on Friday was trading unchanged at $151-1/2 after briefly touching $151 in early London trade.

Citicorp was up $1/4 to $114-5/8 after favourable press comment, dealers said. The Wall Street Journal said on Monday that the second largest U.S. bank was considering going on the acquisition trail in order to compete with rivals.
Elsewhere, PepsiCo rose $1/4 to $37 after press reports that the company planned to reorganise its North American bottling operations by creating a separate unit.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.70 to 851.30 by 1030 GMT while the June U.S. T-bond rose 3/32 to 110-4/32.
